title: No Kings movement holds protests and early voting rallies across Arizona
seoTitle: Phoenix No Kings early voting protests

tea.why: Protesters gathered to reject administration policies, authoritarianism, billionaire-first politics, and the militarization of democracy.
tea.want: Participants demanded democratic change and pushed for early voting, highlighting mail-in ballots and local ballot measures.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Demonstrators gathered in cities across Arizona, including Phoenix, for a nationwide day of action.

summary: On October 17, 2026, participants gathered in cities across Arizona, including Phoenix, Mesa, Tempe, and Tucson, as part of a nationwide "No Kings" day of action. The demonstrations were organized by groups such as Indivisible and the 50501 Movement to oppose the policies and perceived authoritarian actions of the Trump administration. In Phoenix, a main event at Grant Park featured speeches from individuals including U.S. Senator Ruben Gallego, who addressed rising prices and administration policies while encouraging voters to use mail-in ballots. Following the speeches, demonstrators marched to a nearby tabulation box to cast their votes. No official response or counteractions by authorities were reported in the sources.
demands: Promote early voting and mail-in ballot casting
Address rising living costs and policies
response: No official response reported in the sources.
